item.title: HRSS calls for independent probes into enforced disappearances
item.description:
Human rights organization Human Rights Support Society (HRSS) has called for reconsideration of a proposal to keep investigations into enforced disappearance allegations against law enforcement agencies within the law enforcement system itself.
The organization said no agency accused of enforced disappearance, or anybody under its direct control, should be tasked with investigating such allegations. Instead, investigations should be entrusted to an independent investigative body, an independent National Human Rights Commission or a special authority for investigating enforced disappearances.
HRSS made the demand at a meeting held at the Tofazzal Hossain Manik Mia Hall of the National Press Club on Saturday afternoon, ahead of the International Day of the Victims of Enforced Disappearances 2026, which will be observed on Sunday.
The organization described enforced disappearance as a serious human rights violation and said it directly undermines the rule of law, citizens’ security and state accountability.
When a person is detained or abducted by the state, or by a state-authorized or state-backed actor, and authorities deny their whereabouts or conceal their fate and location, it violates not only the individual’s rights to liberty and security but also subjects their family to prolonged uncertainty, mental anguish and denial of justice, HRSS said.
Referring to the final report of the Commission of Inquiry on Enforced Disappearances, formed to investigate allegations of disappearances over an extended period in Bangladesh, HRSS said the commission found that most disappearances were politically motivated.
The investigation also uncovered allegations of involvement by various levels of the security and law enforcement agencies, as well as the existence of a central command structure, it said.
The commission said it had received 1,569 complaints. It also reported that the bodies of 36 people had been recovered following their disappearance, while 251 remained missing.
The commission believed the actual number of enforced disappearances could be higher, HRSS said.
The HRSS meeting also highlighted the disappearance of Miraj Sheikh, a fisherman and motorcycle rider from the Joymoni area of Mongla upazila in Bagerhat, as an example of the current situation.
According to HRSS, Miraj was picked up in plain clothes on April 10 and taken to a local Coast Guard pontoon. Coast Guard members later took him by speedboat towards the Coast Guard base camp in Dighraj.
His family has approached various authorities seeking information about his whereabouts. Published reports also said the High Court ordered authorities to find Miraj and produce him before the court.
According to information collected by HRSS, the incident is the first suspected case of enforced disappearance since July-August 2024.
Against this backdrop, the organization questioned whether an investigation by the police could ensure genuine independence and impartiality if the allegations in Miraj’s case are against the Coast Guard.
Referring to the Enforced Disappearance Prevention and Remedy Ordinance 2025, HRSS said the ordinance had given the National Human Rights Commission an important role in investigating allegations of enforced disappearance.
However, as the ordinance is no longer in effect, the government has initiated the process of formulating a new Enforced Disappearance Prevention and Remedy Act, 2026. The cabinet approved the draft in August 2026.
HRSS said recognizing enforced disappearance as a crime under the proposed law is a positive step. However, the law would fail to achieve its primary objective if it contains serious weaknesses regarding the independence of investigations and protection of victims.
The organization particularly raised concerns over the proposal to entrust law enforcement agencies with investigating allegations of enforced disappearance against law enforcement agencies.
The meeting called for ensuring justice for past enforced disappearances while taking effective legal and institutional measures to prevent such incidents in the present and future.
HRSS said allegations of enforced disappearance between 2009 and 2024 must be investigated promptly, independently and impartially, and those responsible must be brought to justice.
Not only field-level members but also those who issued orders, planned the operations and held responsibility within the chain of command must be held accountable, it said.
The organization also called for clearly defining “command responsibility” in cases of enforced disappearance.
In serious crimes such as enforced disappearance, liability should not be limited to those directly involved, HRSS said. Senior officials who knew or should have known about such crimes but failed to prevent them or take action must also be held accountable under the law.
Before the Enforced Disappearance Prevention and Remedy Act, 2026 is finally passed by parliament, HRSS called for meaningful consultations with civil society, families of victims, lawyers, human rights activists and experts.
The organization also demanded that investigations into allegations against law enforcement agencies be placed under an independent mechanism, punitive provisions that could intimidate complainants be reconsidered, and the safety of victims and witnesses be ensured.
It also called for specific investigation deadlines and accountability for violations of those deadlines.
HRSS further demanded that accused government officials not receive any special immunity during investigations or trials, and that victim families be regularly informed about the progress of investigations.
The organization also called for genuine independence for the National Human Rights Commission.
The commission should be developed as an independent national human rights institution compliant with the Paris Principles rather than being turned into a formal body under government control, HRSS said.
It called for guarantees of the commission’s financial and administrative independence, its authority to appoint its own investigators and conduct independent investigations against security forces, and its power to summon documents and evidence, require witnesses to appear, and inspect detention and custody centers.
HRSS also called for compensation, legal assistance, medical and mental health support, educational assistance and, where necessary, social rehabilitation for victims of enforced disappearance and their families.
The families of victims must also be guaranteed their “right to truth” — the right to know what happened to their loved ones, it said.
The organization demanded that, immediately after any person is detained, their identity, time and place of detention, responsible officer and legal grounds for detention be digitally recorded.
Families and lawyers should be informed promptly, while CCTV, digital custody registers and independent monitoring systems should be installed at all detention and custody centers, it said.
HRSS said justice for enforced disappearances is not a matter of political revenge but a question of state accountability, the rule of law and fundamental rights.
“Justice for past enforced disappearances is essential to preventing future disappearances,” the organization said, calling for a strong law and independent institutions capable of ensuring that no citizen can be made to disappear under the cover of state power.

item.title: PM: Govt committed to fulfilling aspirations of freedom fighters, July martyrs
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on Saturday said the government is committed to realizing the goals and aspirations of the Freedom Fighters (FFs), victims of enforced disappearances, killings and repressions during various democratic movements, as well as the martyrs and victims of the July uprising.
"Sometimes everything cannot be achieved quickly due to various realities, but we will continue our utmost efforts," he said after handing over job appointment letters to 10 members of families affected by enforced disappearances and killings and families of July martyrs at a ceremony at his office in Tejgaon on Saturday afternoon.
A total of 74 people, including members of families affected by enforced disappearances and killings, families of July uprising martyrs and those injured in the July uprising, received appointment letters, with the prime minister personally handing over letters to 10 recipients.
After handing over the appointment letters, the prime minister said, "Today's program is extremely painful for us. We are remembering people who should have been among us today, but sadly they are not. It is through their great sacrifice that the 20-crore people of the country have today been freed from a fascist ruler."
"Only Almighty Allah knows where and in what condition those who are absent among us today are. We should raise our hands and pray to Allah to keep those people in the best possible condition wherever they are," he said.
The prime minister added, "Despite our limited resources, we will make our utmost efforts to stand by the families affected by enforced disappearances and killings and the families of those injured or killed in the July uprising."
"The irreparable losses you have suffered can never be compensated. Yet, we were with you, are with you and will remain with you in the future," he said.
Noting that many of those who made great sacrifices for major national achievements are no longer alive, the prime minister said "To those who are with us, I would say that you made the highest sacrifices for the country and suffered physical harm in various ways. The present government will make every possible effort to fulfil the aspirations for which you risked your lives."
Describing the sacrifices of the democratic fighters as the government's main source of strength and inspiration, Tarique Rahman said, "It is your sacrifices, support and cooperation that give us the courage to work with full vigor. You are our main source of strength and inspiration."
Addressing the families of martyrs, the prime minister sought their continued support and encouragement so that the government could work to fulfil the aspirations of the martyrs and all other democratic fighters for the country and its people.
Family members affected by enforced disappearances and killings and injured persons shared their feelings with prime minister Tarique Rahman at the program, conducted by Atikur Rahman Ruman, also convener of “Amra BNP Paribar”.
Cabinet Secretary Nasimul Gani, Principal Secretary to the Prime Minister ABM Abdus Sattar, Press Secretary AAM Saleh Shibly among others, were present on the occasion.

item.title: Draft law on enforced disappearances awaits National Parliament passage
item.description:
The draft of the proposed “Enforced Disappearance Prevention and Redress Act, 2026," is now available on the website of the Ministry of Home Affairs for public opinion.
After getting public opinion the draft will be given final approval by the National Parliament.
This landmark legislation seeks to fulfill the state's commitment to human rights, individual liberty, and the rule of law which proposed enforced disappearance as a criminal offense and comprehensive punishment.
The draft defines the arrest, detention, or abduction of any individual by a government official or a member of the disciplined forces such as army, navy, air force, police, RAB, BGB, and intelligence agencies followed by a refusal to acknowledge the act or concealment of the victim’s fate as enforced disappearance.
The law explicitly states that enforced disappearance is a ‘continuous offense’, meaning it remains active until the victim's location, condition, or fate is officially confirmed.
Furthermore, no situation, including state security, political instability, or a state of emergency, can be used as a justification for such crime.
Conviction for enforced disappearance carries a maximum life term imprisonment and a fine up to Tk50 lakh.
In case of death of a disappeared person, or if the body is found or remain missing for more than five years, the responsible persons have to face the death penalty or life imprisonment, along with a fine up to Taka one crore.
The draft also proposed a minimum five years in prison for keeping a person confined in a secret detention center or intentional destruction or tampering the evidence related to the disappearance.
A major feature of the law is the introduction of command responsibility. Superiors or commanders of the disciplined forces will be held criminally liable if the disappearance is occurred in their consciousness or they ignored information about this or failed to take steps to prevent it or report it to the authorities. The accountability will also be extended to non-state superiors in relevant cases, the draft said.
The law allowed the victims or witnesses to file lawsuit with the police and in case of any refusal by police the victim can go directly to the court to lodge the complaint.
Investigations must generally be completed within 90 days. Trials of those cases will be held in the court of Sessions Judges and expected to be completed within 90 working days.
The law allows a spouse or children to apply to the court to use or transfer of the property of the missing person in their names to cover essential living expenses and debts.
If a person is missing for five years, a "Disappearance Certificate" can be issued to settle inheritance matters.
The government will maintain a national database of the disappeared persons and establish a Compensation and Rehabilitation Fund for victims and their families.
The draft specifies that the cases involving widespread or systematic disappearances will be tried under the International Crimes (Tribunals) Act, 1973.
Any misuse of the law will make a person responsible for up to five years imprisonment, the draft proposed.

item.title: Nepal rescuers drill for 100 workers trapped in tunnels
item.description:
Nepali army rescue teams were using drilling equipment on Saturday in a race to rescue more than 100 people trapped inside hydropower tunnels, three days after devastating floods struck the site.
“The government has been continuing efforts... to rescue people trapped inside the tunnel of the Trishuli 3A Hydropower Project in Rasuwa,” the office of Nepal’s prime minister said in a statement.
“As part of these efforts, work to clear the tunnel entrance has been intensified since early Saturday morning,” it said.
Those trapped are among 933 missing people who work on hydropower projects on the rivers where a wall of water swept down on Wednesday morning, according to the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority.
The agency said on Thursday that the army had already rescued 350 people under “extremely risky” conditions, but that more than 100 remained trapped.
Initial reports suggested the 100 trapped were in a single location, but officials said that rescue efforts were also underway at other hydropower projects.
Minister of Energy Biraj Bhakta Shrestha said operations were also ongoing at the Trishuli 3B site “despite the adverse weather and extremely challenging circumstances.”
Photographs shared by the disaster office showed workers wading through churned mud and navigating vast boulders left by the floods.
Foreign Minister Shisir Khanal told reporters in Kathmandu that an 11-member Indian expert tunnel rescue team had begun work, and a team from China was “expected to arrive very soon.”
India has extensive experience with difficult Himalayan tunnel rescues, including teams of “rat-hole” miners trained in being able to crawl into narrow spaces.
Khanal said conditions were tough and appealed for assistance, including heavy-lift drones and technology to “help us locate people” who are trapped.
A Nepal Army statement said on Saturday that rescuers were “using equipment including drilling machines in an effort to locate the outer section of the tunnel.”
The US Geological Survey said the disaster on the China-Nepal border on Wednesday was caused by a glacial collapse that created a torrent of debris, with nearly 3,000 people missing and 633 confirmed dead.

item.title: BMD: Rainfall likely to continue over next five days
item.description:
Monsoon remains fairly active over Bangladesh as a low-pressure area forms over the Northwest BayThe Bangladesh Meteorological Department (BMD) has forecast that rainfall is likely to continue across the country over the next five days from 9am on Saturday, as the monsoon remains fairly active over Bangladesh.
“Light to moderate rain or thundershowers, accompanied by temporary gusty winds, are likely to occur at many places over Rangpur, Mymensingh, Chittagong and Sylhet divisions and at a few places over Rajshahi, Dhaka, Khulna and Barisal divisions, with moderately heavy falls at places across the country,” said a regular bulletin of the Met office.
Day and night temperatures may remain nearly unchanged across the country.
A low-pressure area has formed over the Northwest Bay and adjoining West Bengal-North Odisha coasts. It is likely to move west-northwestwards.
The axis of the monsoon trough runs through Rajasthan, Punjab, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh and Bihar, with one end extending to Assam across the southern part of Bangladesh through the centre of the low-pressure area.
The monsoon is fairly active over Bangladesh and strong over the North Bay.

item.title: Agriculture minister: No shortage of fertilizer, action if artificial crisis created
item.description:
Agriculture and Fisheries and Livestock Minister Mohammed Aminur Rashid on Saturday said the country has sufficient fertiliser supplies and warned that strict action would be taken against anyone found creating an artificial shortage or charging farmers excessive prices.
He made the remarks at a meeting with government officials at the deputy commissioner’s office in Faridpur.
Faridpur Deputy Commissioner Mazharul Islam presided over the meeting.
The minister said the country imports 1.5 million tonnes more fertiliser than its total demand, leaving no scope for a shortage.
He said some fertilizer retailers are spreading rumours that fertiliser is unavailable in the market while supplying it when offered extra money.
The minister said the government is farmer-friendly and will do whatever is necessary for the development of farmers.“The government believes that the country will progress if farmers prosper.”
He said the quality of soil in the country has deteriorated for various reasons, but Faridpur’s soil is still among the best in the country.
Such fertile soil is difficult to find in many other districts, creating significant opportunities to further develop agriculture in Faridpur, he added.
The minister said the government is working to stop imports of jute and onion seeds in the future.
He said another major government target in agriculture is to reduce imports of agricultural products and meet domestic demand through increased local production.
“Our main target is to ensure that we do not have to import any agricultural products in the future. We are trying to produce them ourselves. Everyone concerned will have to work hard and make efforts to achieve this,” he said.
He instructed dealers to play a responsible role in ensuring that fertiliser reaches farmers on time and at fair prices.
Director General of the Department of Agricultural Extension Mohammad Abdur Rahim, Faridpur, Additional Superintendent of Police Fatema Islam, Additional Deputy Commissioner Sohrab Hossain and Deputy Director of the Department of Agricultural Extension agriculturist Shahaduzzaman, among others, attended the meeting.

item.title: 17 banks pledge Tk17,000cr to revive closed factories
item.description:
Seventeen commercial banks have joined hands with Bangladesh Bank to fund a Tk41,000 crore credit pool aimed at restarting long-shuttered industrial plants, driving private investment, and lifting the economy out of its recent slump.
The commitment forms the backbone of a broader Tk60,000 crore stimulus package first unveiled by the central bank on May 23.
Under the agreement, participating commercial lenders will cover Tk41,000 crore of the total allocation, while Bangladesh Bank will finance the remaining Tk19,000 crore directly from its internal reserves.
The participating institutions include a mix of state-owned and leading private lenders: Sonali Bank, Agrani Bank, Rupali Bank, Brac Bank, City Bank, Jamuna Bank, Dutch-Bangla Bank, Mutual Trust Bank, Uttara Bank, Prime Bank, Bank Asia, NCC Bank, Pubali Bank, Eastern Bank, Mercantile Bank, Trust Bank, and Southeast Bank.
At the heart of the initiative is a dedicated Tk20,000 crore allotment—the package's largest single component—specifically targeted at getting dormant factories back into operation.
Private entrepreneurs will be eligible to tap into these funds via loans carrying an average interest rate of 7.5%.
Terming the scheme a core "Production and Employment Recovery" program, Bangladesh Bank Governor Md Mostakur Rahman noted during a recent press briefing that the central bank expects the initiative to generate nearly 2.5 million new jobs.
Beyond immediate employment, financial regulators anticipate that restoring closed production lines will catalyze broader private sector investment and supply the momentum needed to break the economy's ongoing stagnation.

item.title: Measles outbreak: Death toll reaches 963 as three die in 24 hours
item.description:
Three more children have died from measles-like symptoms in the 24 hours leading up to 8:00am on Saturday, raising the overall death toll from the ongoing outbreak to 963.
With the latest figures, the total number of suspected measles deaths has reached 864, while the number of confirmed deaths remained unchanged at 99, as no new confirmed measles deaths were reported in the last 24 hours.
The Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) has classified all three of the latest casualties as suspected.
Among the three new suspected fatalities, the highest concentration was recorded in Dhaka, with two deaths reported in both the Dhaka division and Dhaka district.
A total of 886 suspected measles cases were recorded in the 24 hours till Saturday morning, taking the overall suspected case tally to 155,678.
During the same period, 57 new confirmed measles cases were reported, bringing the total number of confirmed infections to 18,853.
Since March 15, 2026, a total of 136,257 suspected measles patients have been hospitalized across the country, of whom 131,264 have recovered and been discharged from hospitals, according to the DGHS.

item.title: Headteacher dies after falling from rickshaw during mugging near parliament
item.description:
A primary school head teacher died after falling from a rickshaw when two muggers allegedly snatched her bag near the South Plaza of the National Parliament building in Dhaka on Saturday morning.
The incident occurred around 6:30am at the South Plaza.
The deceased was identified as Ranjina Parvin, head teacher of Bagbari Girls’ Government Primary School in Bogra.
According to information available, Ranjina had travelled from Bogra overnight to see a doctor at Islamia Eye Hospital in Farmgate. She got off at Gabtoli bus terminal at dawn and then took a rickshaw towards the hospital.
When the rickshaw reached the South Plaza of the Parliament building, the muggers allegedly approached from behind on a motorcycle and snatched her bag. She fell from the rickshaw and sustained a head injury.
She was rescued from the scene and taken to Shaheed Suhrawardy Medical College Hospital where the doctor on duty declared her dead.
Tejgaon Division Deputy Commissioner (DC) Ibne Mizan said police were working to identify the motorcycle and those involved.
He expressed hope that the suspects would be identified and arrested within a short time.

item.title: Nepal-China flood: Death toll reaches 633, missing near 3,000
item.description:
Rescuers in Nepal and China were battling Saturday to locate thousands of people missing days after a deadly, tsunami-like wall of water and debris swept through the Himalayan region, engulfing entire villages.
The latest figures from both countries put the number of missing close to 3,000, with 633 bodies recovered -- and reports of some dead possibly swept downstream as far away as India.
Rescue worker Kawan Koirala, from the Nepal Scout Disaster Response Team, said they were struggling in thick, leg-sucking mud.
“People want their family’s body back, either dead or alive, but we cannot find them... you can see the mud,” he told AFP, exhausted after an 18-hour shift.
“It is very traumatic for me too. It is my first time seeing these types of things. Everywhere is mud. We faced floods in Nepal before, but not like this.”
The US Geological Survey said the disaster on Wednesday on the Tibet-Nepal border was caused by a glacial collapse that created a torrent of debris downstream.
Survivors face an agonizing wait to learn the fate of missing relatives, and the prospect of rebuilding their lives from nothing.
“All the settlements near the river were swept away,” Buddhi Ram Dangol told AFP in Nepal’s Nuwakot district. “There is nothing left.”
At Bidur’s army base, a key rescue hub in the same district, relatives crowded around lists of rescued people pasted on a wall.
“I have come here looking for my son,” said Kalka Sharda, scanning the list in desperation. “He was a laborer at the hydropower plant, but I can’t find his name, and the authorities are not saying anything.”
In an area home to vast energy infrastructure projects, Nepal’s disaster authority listed 933 hydropower workers among the missing, along with 517 foreigners, including trekkers and pilgrims to Tibet’s sacred Mount Kailash.
The trauma of Wednesday’s catastrophe has been “enormous,” and as many as 93,000 people may have been affected, the Red Cross said, with the death toll expected to rise.
Emergency teams worked flat out to find survivors as widespread devastation left communities short of food and water.
Fears of further flooding have compounded the search for the missing.
The deluge of ice and mud caused huge lakes, and one of these formations has become a risk of further floods.
While the exact cause of the collapse is unclear, climate change is causing glaciers to melt worldwide, increasing the risks of such disasters.
In Tibet, where Chinese authorities are the only source of information, Beijing had paused its rescue operation at the hardest-hit area of Gyirong over the risk of renewed flooding.
On the Nepali side, soldiers were trying desperately to drill through to 100 people trapped in the tunnel of the Trishuli 3A hydropower project on Saturday.
The prime minister’s office said teams had begun “clearing mud and debris” to open the entrance, while a specialized Indian tunnel rescue unit had arrived to help.
Workers rescued from other dam projects along the Trishuli valley described a disaster that unfolded with terrifying speed.
Nepal reported a death toll of 626 people on Saturday.
There are 2,426 people, including hundreds of foreigners, who are out of contact in the country.
Across the border in Tibet, which is largely inaccessible to foreign journalists, seven people died and 554 remain missing, the state Xinhua news agency said Saturday.
Authorities also said they had evacuated 555 stranded tourists and 499 Chinese residents from Tibet.
In India, authorities said they had recovered seven bodies from rivers flowing from Nepal, believed to be flood victims.
Scores of Hindu devotees from across the world are among those missing on the border, as many were on a pilgrimage to Tibet’s Mount Kailash.
Sivaranjani Muthunathan was travelling by bus with 56 others towards the Chinese border when they became stuck in what they thought was a traffic jam.
“Then there was fog, smoke, something that seemed to suddenly engulf us,” Muthunathan, 46, told AFP on Friday, showing a phone video she recorded of a torrent surging towards her.
Around them, vehicles were swept away or buried under mud.
“One by one, we also climbed out through the driver’s side,” then scrambled up a hill, she said.

item.title: PM Tarique hands job appointment letters to families of movement victims
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on Saturday handed over job appointment letters to family members of those who were subjected to enforced disappearance or killed during the movement against the Awami League government, as well as families of those killed in the July mass uprising.
The appointment letters were handed over at an event held at the Karabi Hall of the Prime Minister’s Tejgaon Office in Dhaka around noon.
Family members of the victims and officials from various levels of the government attended the event.
Several recipients became emotional after receiving their appointment letters. The prime minister assured them that he would always stand by them.
The program was conducted by the Prime Minister’s Additional Press Secretary Atikur Rahman Rumon.

item.title: Law minister: Govt to decide on Makkah Pact after considering all aspects
item.description:
Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs Minister Md Asaduzzaman has said the government will decide whether Bangladesh will join the Makkah Pact after considering all aspects of the matter.
He made the remarks on Saturday while responding to questions from journalists after attending a reception for meritorious students of Jhenidah Collectorate School and College as the chief guest.
Deputy Commissioner Md Noman Hossain presided over the program, while Prime Minister’s Political Assistant Rashed Khan attended as the special guest.
The law minister said India would act according to its foreign policy, while Bangladesh would follow its own policy.
“India will move like India, and Bangladesh will move like Bangladesh,” he added.
Regarding the country’s law and order situation, Asaduzzaman said the issue was not whether the government was satisfied with the situation, but whether it was making relentless efforts to maintain normalcy.
He said the government and the Ministry of Law are also working to introduce e-judiciary to digitalize the country’s judicial system.
The government plans to implement the e-judiciary system within the next year, he added.
District BNP President MA Majid, General Secretary Zahiduzzaman Mona, Vice-President Munshi Kamal Azad Pannu, Joint General Secretary Abdul Majid Biswas and Shailkupa upazila BNP General Secretary Humayun Babar Firoz, among other BNP leaders and activists of its affiliated organizations, attended the reception.

item.title: Nepali families search at a Kathmandu noticeboard for news of missing loved ones
item.description:
Photographs of unidentified dead plaster the walls of a major hospital in Kathmandu.
The pictures are printed on A4 paper, displayed in the hope someone will recognize them.
But the rain regularly arrives before a loved one can — streaking and washing away the faces, forcing them to be reprinted.
Rescuers in the areas hardest hit in Nepal’s catastrophic flash flooding have to prioritize survivors. They cannot bring all the bodies back, so photos are taken instead.
Hanging alongside the pictures of the lost is a noticeboard with lists of survivors and the injured.
Crowds of people gather at the gates of the Tribhuvan University Teaching Hospital desperately hoping they will find their loved ones on the latter.
Almost 3000 people are now missing in Nepal after a glacial collapse sent a wall of water, mud and debris tearing through the valley on the border with Tibet, wiping out communities.
Some 633 bodies have been recovered on the Nepali side.
Hung next to the pictures of the deceased are smiling photos of those who are missing — remnants of better days.
Friends and family are taking matters into their own hands, posting pictures of the people they are searching for.
Police and volunteers are set up at desks taking the names and numbers of those who have missing relatives.
Some people come here multiple times a day in the desperate hope they will receive good news.
Among the crowd at the hospital is Tilmaya Gurung. She has been visiting hospitals and morgues in the city searching for news of her sister’s husband.
Meg Bahadur was working at a hydropower plant in Rasuwa when the flood hit. The 49-year-old has two children.
“We tried his phone several times but his phone is not connecting,” she wept.
“We came here to hospital to check the list pasted here but not found his name on the list.”
Her husband Jai Bahadur Gurung explained that the relatives split into groups to go to different sites to search for information.
He is trying to remain hopeful, but as the days stretch on the fear is building.
“We are here at hospital looking among dead,” he said.
More than 400 injured people, airlifted from the disaster area, have been brought here.
Chief of the emergency medicine department Ramesh Kumar Maharjan said most of those patients had been buried in mud.
“People were buried from head to toe and they have chest injuries and limb injuries, fractures, as well as head injuries and aspiration,” he said.
“They were crushed. Their chests were crushed. They had become trapped.”
He said some of the people that had recovered from suffocation had “mud trapped inside them.”
Staff have never treated patients like this before and are having to develop new methods, including a “decontamination shower” to remove the mud.
One of his patients is a five-year-old girl who had lost all of her family members. She is in critical care with a head injury.
This region is prone to natural disasters. It’s been hit with earthquakes and more standard flooding before. But Dr Maharjan said this was a “different type of natural disaster” altogether.
The flooding has destroyed roads and bridges, meaning the worst hit areas are only accessible by helicopter.
It is not only making it difficult to get injured people out, it is also making it difficult to get aid in.
Less than 10 kilometres from the hospital, at a specialist hub, people are loading trucks with supplies like hygiene kits, food, water, and protective equipment.
Hangers are lined up, filled with donations from all over the world.
The humanitarian staging area was already set up, built on experiences with previous natural disasters, and in some areas allowed supplies to arrive within five hours of the emergency being declared.
But getting aid to those most in need is incredibly difficult.
UN World Food Program country director Riaz Lodhi said road access being cut to the worst hit areas was “very restrictive” and made it difficult to assess the situation.
“We still don’t know what the needs are out there,” he said.
Aid supplies are currently being trucked a certain distance before being transferred to helicopter to be flown in.
“It’s an enormous challenge given the magnitude of the disaster,” he said.

item.title: India’s citizen-led school audits test limits of activism
item.description:
The Indian activist movement dubbing itself the “Cockroach Janta Party (CJP)” shot to national prominence in May by leading weeks-long protests over a scandal involving highly competitive entrance exams.
The student-led campaign put the government under intense political pressure and ended with the resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan in July.
Now, the CJP is taking aim at India’s government schools, organizing volunteer visits to classrooms, documenting conditions and demanding accountability for problems.
Launched on August 15, Independence Day in India, the campaign asks parents, students and volunteers to inspect schools and record basic facilities including toilets, drinking water, electricity, classroom furniture and school buildings. The CJP has said the findings will be used to pressure authorities to make improvements.
The initial target is to audit 100 rural government schools over two months. It has also proposed giving recognition to village leaders who improve their schools.
Unlike the first campaign, which was based on street protests, the school audits require a more sustained form of local activism. Volunteers are expected to work consistently at the local level, document conditions and follow up with officials, parents and communities.
The organization is dealing with different layers of the Indian administration. Responsibility for government schools is divided between state governments, local administrations and elected village bodies. The CJP is therefore set to tackle different rules and political interests across the country.
India has over a million government schools, according to Education Ministry data. They make up nearly 70% of all schools in the country but serve less than half of its 247 million schoolchildren.
That scale has given CJP a vast field for its campaign. But it has also brought a new set of challenges.
The authorities are raising questions regarding rules and locations for the CJP scrutiny, as well as safeguards when children are present.
The response is already varying from state to state. Some authorities have ordered their own inspections, while others have restricted access or taken police action against CJP volunteers.
Authorities in Maharashtra and Rajasthan states have objected to school visits carried out without permission.
In one case, a complaint by school authorities resulted in police action against CJP members after they entered the premises to conduct an audit.
In Rajasthan, restrictions have been imposed on outsiders entering government schools, as well as on filming, interviews and other forms of documentation. CJP volunteers in Rajasthan have also said they were attacked while inspecting a school.
“We are not afraid. We are seeking accountability from the government,” said CJP spokesperson Ashutosh Ranka.
In the state of Uttar Pradesh, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath has ordered officials to conduct on-the-spot checks of school facilities and directed police to register cases over what he called misleading videos about schools and colleges.
The CJP has said such measures undermine public scrutiny. Authorities have said schools are not open spaces for unauthorized inspections, particularly when children are present.
Vinita Gursahani Singh, managing trustee of We, The People campaign, which works on citizen empowerment, said the limits are set by law.
“Under the Right to Information Act, any citizen can inspect schools but you need to submit an application. And that makes sense as there has to be consideration for students and teaching,” Singh told DW.
“All public scrutiny is legitimate. It is our job to scrutinize. But the scrutiny has to follow process. It has to be even-handed. What applies to one citizen must apply to all,” she said.
The CJP maintains government schools are publicly funded institutions and citizens have a legitimate right to ask how they are functioning.
Its volunteers use standardized audit forms to record conditions and send their findings to the CJP, which has said it will use the material to press local administrations to respond.
But critics question whether citizen activists can assume the role of inspectors. There are concerns about whether volunteers have the expertise to assess safety or infrastructure problems and how allegations posted on social media are verified.
Mohandas Pai, an education advocate, supports CJP’s focus on government schools but disagrees with its methods.

item.title: Zimbabwe crash involving church minibus kills 27
item.description:
A minibus carrying churchgoers collided head-on with a truck in central Zimbabwe, killing at least 27 people, police said Saturday, in the latest deadly road crash to hit the country.
The crash occurred at around 1830 GMT on Friday near Chivhu, about 140 kilometres (87 miles) south of the capital Harare, police said.
The foreign-registered haulage truck was overtaking another vehicle when it collided with the minibus, which was carrying worshippers to a conference.
Both vehicles were carrying an “unknown” number of passengers, police said. Seven people were injured in the crash.
Footage shared on social media by public broadcaster ZBC showed the mangled minibus charred to a shell, with the truck coming to rest on the opposite side of the road.
The crash occurred in a flat, remote stretch of road, with low vegetation lining the roadside and open terrain beyond.
Traffic accidents are common in Zimbabwe, where roads are riddled with potholes due to years of underfunding and neglect, and driving standards can be poor.
For everyday transport, many Zimbabweans rely on the privately run minibus taxis, known locally as kombi, but they are often criticized for overloading.
In April, at least 18 people were killed when a minibus burst into flames on a highway in the south, while earlier that month a woman and her five children died when their vehicle collided with a haulage truck on another highway linking Zimbabwe and South Africa.

item.title: Alcaraz anxious after layoff but feels 'great' about wrist
item.description:
Carlos Alcaraz said Friday he feels at "100 percent" ahead of his defense of the US Open, but acknowledged feeling anxious after a four-month layoff due to a wrist injury.
The Spaniard has drawn confidence from grueling practice sessions ahead of the Grand Slam, he told reporters at a pre-tournament media day.
"I need to come here to practice with these guys to feel the competition once again, and this is really testing," he said.
"I'm feeling great and ... that helped me a lot to to know right now that it's all in my head," he said.
Alcaraz, 23, the youngest player to win the career Grand Slam after triumphing in Australia in January, hasn't played singles since April 16, withdrawing from the Barcelona Open with a right wrist injury and subsequently skipping both the French Open and Wimbledon.
Alcaraz, who partnered Serena Williams in the US Open's mixed doubles event on Tuesday, told reporters on Friday that his coaching and support team had complete confidence that he was ready to go.
"I gotta trust my people that tell me that it's gonna be fine. So I just have to go 100 percent," he said. "So I'm just trying to to like stay away ... from that fear."
Alcaraz will open his defense against Russian veteran Roman Safiullin.
Should he clear that and the subsequent two matches, he could face a potential fourth round match with Tommy Paul or Alexander Bublik, with potentially either Ben Shelton or Arthur Fils looming in the quarterfinals.
The Spanish star would normally be an automatic favorite to win again in New York. But the injury has made him more of a question mark in 2026.
Other top players are not discounting Alcaraz' chances.
"I expect him to be maybe a bit rusty the first or second match, but once he gets through that, I think he's going to be a contender for sure here," said second-ranked Alexander Zverev, the top seed due to the withdrawal of world number one Jannik Sinner.
Coming back after a layoff at a Grand Slam where men play three out of five sets is "not necessarily easy to do," said American Taylor Fritz, the ninth seed.
"But, you know, if you can get past those first couple of rounds, you start to feel pretty good," Fritz said. "Then at that point there's no reason why he couldn't, you know, find form and play really well. Who knows?"
- Sinner rivalry on hiatus -
Fans reacted rapturously to Alcaraz' brief partnership with Williams, with the superstar pair winning their first match before losing soundly in the second round to Belinda Bencic of Switzerland and Flavio Cobolli of Italy.
While Alcaraz showed flashes of brilliance, he looked rusty at times, with some pundits also noting that his serve lacked its customary pop.
In 2025, Alcaraz and Sinner split the four Grand Slams with each winning two. The two young stars have been the most bankable champions since the generation of Roger Federer, Rafael Nadal and Novak Djokovic, the only one of three older greats still playing and a contender in New York.
But after Alcaraz and Sinner met in the finals of three slams in 2025, they will not face off in any of the biggest events in 2026 after Sinner's withdrawal from New York due to a knee injury.
"We are not gonna see each other for, like, six months now, seven months. So it's kind of weird situation, to be honest," Alcaraz said of his rival.
"I just wish him all the best. Hopefully a really great recovery and see him back on court at his best once again."
Alcaraz acknowledged that being out of competition was difficult, particularly early on when he couldn't use his arm, he made the most of the break.
"At the same time, I enjoyed my time," he said. "I enjoyed my time with family, with friends, staying at home."
In July, Alcaraz appeared in New York at the World Cup final to watch his native Spain defeat Argentina.
"It was a really cool experience and really cool moment," he said of the appearance, while calling the chance to see Spain win their second World Cup "a lifetime experience."

item.title: Bayern steamroll Stuttgart in Bundesliga opener
item.description:
Michael Olise and Luis Diaz were among five goalscorers as Bayern Munich cruised to a 5-1 home win over Stuttgart in Friday's Bundesliga opener.
Defending Bundesliga champions Bayern were in control from start to finish in a rematch of last season's German Cup final, with Olise in spectacular form despite the greasy conditions in the Bavarian capital.
Dayot Upamecano headed the hosts in front from a corner and while Josha Vagnoman levelled things up for Stuttgart after the break, Bayern scored twice in three minutes through Olise and a Vagnomann own goal to restore control.
Bundesliga debutant Ismael Saibari created a late goal for Aleksandar Pavlovic and Diaz scored in stoppage time to extend Bayern's unbeaten run in league openers to 15 seasons.
"He relies heavily on intuition, reacting before the opponent does," Bayern defender Konrad Laimer said of Olise.
"It's an incredible quality, especially in one-on-one situations. You need that instinct to read the situation: knowing when to pass, when to dribble, and when to shoot.
"It's really fun to be out there on the pitch with him."
With 14 goals including three hat-tricks, Harry Kane had scored against Stuttgart more than any other German opponent but had a quiet night and was subbed out late in the second-half.
The big win will likely see Bayern top the table after matchday one, extending their streak to 67 matchdays dating back to September 2024.
Bayern lost just one of 40 domestic matches last year but coach Vincent Kompany said it was his job to keep the squad hungry.
"Everything starts again from zero. I hope all players are aware of that, but it's also my role to instill it into them."
- 'Lights out' for Stuttgart -
Stuttgart coach Sebastian Hoeness revealed the players were left in the dark at half-time due to a power outage.
"The lights were out," Hoeness said, adding "but we could still see each other. We didn't trip over.
"Bayern will beat plenty of other teams here, maybe by more, but we have to improve, no question about it."
Before the match, Germany coach Jurgen Klopp told Sky he had told Bayern midfielder Jamal Musiala "the door is open for you" as he continues to return from a neurological condition from which he collapsed twice in pre-season fixtures.
Vincent Kompany made two changes to the side which won 2-1 at Borussia Dortmund in the Supercup, including returning France centre-back Upamecano to the starting XI.
Both sides started well despite the teeming rain, with Stuttgart's Tiago Tomas and Olise hitting the woodwork early.
Upamecano put Bayern in front in simple fashion with 21 minutes gone, leaping high to glance in a Kimmich corner.
Early in the second-half, Stuttgart got themselves back in the match when Vagnoman blasted in a rebound, but Bayern quickly reclaimed the initiative.
Olise converted an expert Kimmich pass from close range just three minutes before Vagnoman scored at how own end of the pitch, slipping when trying to clear a low Alphonso Davies cross.
Olise had the ball in the net again just six minutes later when he turned in a clever Kane through ball, but his goal was chalked off for a narrow offside.
Saibari cut back for Pavlovic to score late and Diaz added another in stoppage time to round out a comprehensive win.

item.title: Marquinhos rescues last-gasp draw for PSG at Lille in Ligue 1
item.description:
Captain Marquinhos headed in a dramatic last-gasp equaliser as Paris Saint-Germain scored twice in stoppage time to snatch a 2-2 draw at Lille in Ligue 1 on Friday.
It looked as though the reigning French and European champions were heading for defeat as goals by Hakon Haraldsson and Dilane Bakwa for Lille left PSG trailing 2-0 with the 90 minutes up.
But a Vitinha strike in the first added minute gave Luis Enrique's team sudden belief. The Portugal playmaker then crossed for Marquinhos to head in with the final act of the game in northern France.
It was a cruel blow for Lille and their new coach Davide Ancelotti, who worked with Marquinhos as part of the Brazil staff at the recent World Cup.
"It is never finished against PSG," said Marquinhos.
PSG remain without a victory at the start of this Ligue 1 season but this was the second successive game in which they had come from two behind late on to grab a share of the spoils.
Last weekend they trailed 2-0 away to Rennes before Spain's World Cup final hero Ferran Torres came off the bench and netted a brace to earn a point.
"It says a lot about us," added Marquinhos. "The positive thing is our mentality, and our ability to come back and get a result from behind. That augurs well for the rest of the season."
- Dembele left out -
Torres, a new arrival from Barcelona, had replaced Ousmane Dembele at half-time in Rennes, and the French international was then told by his manager to go away and have this week off.
He was therefore not involved here, while another of France's World Cup stars Bradley Barcola was also absent with a huge-money transfer to Liverpool understood to be imminent.
Khvicha Kvaratskhelia was also benched at kick-off for the visitors, who saw Achraf Hakimi come close to giving them an early lead with an effort which grazed the post.
Haraldsson then struck in stunning fashion just before the midway point in the first half for Lille, who this week sold prodigious teenage talent Ayyoub Bouaddi to Manchester City for an initial 100 million euros ($117m).
The Icelandic international midfielder scored with a thumping first-time effort from the edge of the area after a brilliant reverse pass by Olivier Giroud to set him up.
Kvaratskhelia and summer recruit Mika Godts both came on in the second half for PSG, but they were reeling when Bakwa -- just on for his debut after joining on loan from Nottingham Forest -- curled in for 2-0 with six minutes left.
It seemed set to be two wins out of two for Lille under new Italian coach, whose father Carlo Ancelotti -- the current Brazil boss -- watched from the stands at the Stade Pierre-Mauroy.
Davide Ancelotti was on the staff at PSG when Carlo was in charge of the Qatar-owned club between 2012 and 2013.
But PSG's late show denied them, and Luis Enrique's side will take confidence from their remarkable comeback here as they prepare for the upcoming defence of their Champions League title.
"At this point in the season it would be very dangerous to be at 100 percent already," said the coach.
The two-time reigning European champions, who have already beaten Aston Villa to claim this season's UEFA Super Cup, will notably play Barcelona and Manchester City in the league phase of the Champions League.
Elsewhere in Ligue 1 this weekend, last season's runners-up Lens go to Strasbourg on Saturday, while Monaco face Marseille on Sunday.

item.title: Cherki makes his point to Maresca as Man City sparkle in Palace rout
item.description:
Rayan Cherki proved his point to Enzo Maresca as the Manchester City star's brilliant double inspired a 4-1 rout of Crystal Palace on Friday.
City boss Maresca admitted Cherki was frustrated to be left out of the starting line-up for last weekend's 2-1 win against Bournemouth in their Premier League opener.
The France playmaker responded to the snub in emphatic style.
He came off the bench to provide a pair of assists against Bournemouth and seized his chance to start at Selhurst Park with a masterful display that underlined his qualities.
The 23-year-old had alarmed Pep Guardiola with some of his more flamboyant antics on the pitch in his debut season at City last term, while questions remain about the former Lyon midfielder's ability to adhere to a team-first ethos.
But Cherki's talent is undeniable, as he showed with his brace after an own goal from City keeper Gianluigi Donnarumma had cancelled out Erling Haaland's opener in rainy south London.
Haaland struck again in the closing stages to cap City's dominant display as the Norway striker scored his first goals since cutting off his famous blond locks in favour of a close-cropped hair style last week.
In a glimpse into what City hope is a bright future after Guardiola, teenage Morocco midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi, signed from Lille for £86 million ($116 million) this week, came off the bench for his debut in the closing minutes.
City came from behind to beat Bournemouth thanks to late goals from Marc Guehi and Josko Gvardiol in the opening league match of the post-Guardiola era.
But, with Cherki in the groove and Haaland in lethal mood, there was no need for any last-gasp dramatics against Palace.
It was Palace's second successive defeat under new manager Pierre Sage, who replaced Oliver Glasner in the close-season.
Having used Guehi out of position as a midfielder against Bournemouth, Maresca moved the England international to his preferred centre-back role against his former club.
Nico O'Reilly did a capable job of filling the central midfield berth alongside Elliot Anderson, who improved after a disappointing debut against Bournemouth.
Anderson should have bagged his first goal for City after a corner sparked a goal-mouth scramble that included blocked shots for the midfielder and Haaland.
Haaland made amends in typically predatory fashion in the 17th minute.
Antoine Semenyo's cross was flighted perfectly for Haaland to rise above the Palace defence and guide a superb header over Eagles keeper Dean Henderson.
Phil Foden wasted a chance to double City's lead when the forward scuffed wide from Anderson's pass.
He was guilty of an even worse miss moments later, miscuing his header after Cherki picked him out inside the six-yard box.
Cherki's low drive was repelled by Henderson on the stroke of half-time.
Palace striker Eddie Nketiah let City off the hook with a wayward finish immediately after the interval.
Cherki took charge after that, making Palace pay in the 54th minute.
Foden's driving run teed up Cherki, who slalomed past three Palace defenders before applying the finishing touch to a sublime move as he slotted into the far corner.
Palace thought they had earned a lifeline two minutes later when Yeremy Pino's free-kick hit the post and rebounded into the net off Donnarumma's back.
Cherki extinguished Palace's revival in the 59th minute, unleashing a fierce strike from the edge of the area that fizzed past Henderson's out-stretched hand.
Haaland sealed the demolition in the 84th minute, drilling past Henderson from an acute angle after Foden's pass shredded the Palace defence.

item.title: Ramos strikes as AC Milan beat Venezia
item.description:
Star signing Goncalo Ramos scored with a flashing drive from a tight angle for his first Serie A goal as AC Milan beat Venezia 2-0 at the San Siro on Friday.
Milan spent 74mn euros to acquire Ramos from Paris Saint-Germain and the Portuguese delivered a goal to treasure on 69 minutes before a late own goal from Redouane Halhal settled the game.
"The most important thing isn't my goal, it's the win," Ramos said adding "I should have scored more than one goal tonight."Milan opened the season with a 2-1 win away at Torino making Friday's encounter their first home game since Franco Baresi died with hommage paid to their former skipper ahead of kick off.
New boss Ruben Amorim watched his big close-season signing Ramos fluff a first minute effort that came at him too close to his feet, but his opener from the left of the box lifted the home crowd as the striker reeled away in joy.
"We're starting to show this team's DNA and mindset; I already feel right at home in this group," said Ramos.
A break from the half-way line and shot from the edge of the box from substitute Ardon Jashari on 89 minutes came off the Venezia goalkeeper, hit the onrushing defender Halhal's knee and flew home to make it 2-0.
Milan are rebuilding under former Manchester United boss Amorim after missing Champions League qualification of the final day of last season.
Juventus host Parma in Saturday's late Serie A game. Italy's Champions League quartet are in action later. On Sunday when Como take their ambitions to Napoli, champions Inter Milan travel to Cagliari. Roma play at Lecce on Monday.

item.title: Gold price drops by Tk7,109 per bhori
item.description:
The price of 22-carat gold has been reduced by Tk7,109 per bhori in Bangladesh, with the new rate coming into effect from 10am on Saturday, according to the Bangladesh Jewellers Association (Bajus).
Under the new rate, 22-carat gold will cost Tk20,630 per gram, or Tk240,636 per bhori (11.664 grams), including VAT. The previous price was Tk247,745 per bhori.
The decision was taken at a meeting of Bajus's Standing Committee on Pricing and Price Monitoring on Saturday morning, following a decline in the price of Tejabi gold (pure gold) and silver in the local market.
According to the new rates, 21-carat gold has been priced at Tk19,700 per gram, while 18-carat gold will cost Tk16,920 per gram. Gold under the traditional system has been set at Tk13,820 per gram.
On a per-bhori basis, 21-carat gold will cost approximately Tk229,891, 18-carat gold Tk197,333 and traditional-system gold approximately Tk161,173.
Bajus has also reduced the price of silver.
The new price of 22-carat silver has been set at Tk455 per gram, 21-carat at Tk435, 18-carat at Tk375 and traditional-system silver at Tk285 per gram.
The previous price of 22-carat silver was Tk470 per gram, meaning it has fallen by Tk15 per gram.
On Tuesday, Bajus had set the price of 22-carat gold at Tk21,240 per gram, or Tk247,745 per bhori.
At the time, 21-carat gold was priced at Tk20,285 per gram, 18-carat at Tk17,420 and traditional-system gold at Tk14,225 per gram.
Bajus had also raised gold prices on August 22. The latest reduction comes after several changes in gold prices in the final week of August.
Bajus said VAT is included in the announced selling prices, so customers cannot be charged VAT separately. However, making charges will be added depending on the design of the jewellery.
The association also said its existing rules will remain in effect for the exchange, purchase and sale of gold and silver jewellery, excluding VAT, making charges and the value of stones.
The new prices will remain effective at all jewellery shops across the country until further notice from Bajus.

item.title: Chief justice warns against use of AI in court judgments
item.description:
Chief Justice Zubayer Rahman Chowdhury has warned that artificial intelligence (AI) must not be used to write court judgments.
He made the remarks while inaugurating the country’s first AI Governance Summer School at the Asiatic Society Bangladesh auditorium in Dhaka on Saturday.
The chief justice said AI cannot be used to assess the subject matter of cases, relevant laws and provisions, facts and evidence, or a judge’s conscience. He therefore urged caution in using AI in judicial decision-making.
He also called for effective laws and policies to determine where and to what extent AI can be used.
“AI must be used to make people’s lives easier and protect fundamental rights,” he said.
The chief justice said training and skills were more important than infrastructure in ensuring the effective use of AI.
He also warned that using information generated by AI without proper verification could be risky.

item.title: Traffic movement returns to normal on Dhaka-Chittagong highway
item.description:
Traffic movement on the Dhaka-Chittagong highway has returned to normal after a covered van broke down in the Narayanganj section, causing a traffic jam stretching about 1km.
The congestion occurred on the Chittagong-bound lane in the Pirojpur Union area on Saturday morning. Highway police later removed the vehicle, restoring normal traffic flow.
According to highway police and local sources, a large pothole developed on the Dhaka-bound section of the highway in the Ashari Char area following recent heavy rain. Urgent repair work was subsequently undertaken.
A pothole measuring about five metres wide was filled with micro-concrete, forcing authorities to close one lane from Friday morning until Saturday morning. The lane was reopened after the repair work was completed.
Meanwhile, the covered van broke down on the Chittagong-bound lane in the Pirojpur Union area on Saturday morning, causing congestion for about 1km. The traffic jam extended to the Meghna Toll Plaza.
Upon receiving the information, highway police removed the vehicle and traffic movement returned to normal.
Rubel Hossain, a passenger from Sonargaon’s Mograpara area, said: “There is no traffic jam here now. A covered van broke down in the Pirojpur Union area of the highway, causing congestion.”
Kachpur Highway Police Station Officer-in-Charge Shamim Sheikh confirmed the matter, saying a temporary traffic jam occurred after the covered van broke down.
“Upon receiving the information, highway police removed the vehicle. Traffic movement has now returned to normal,” he said.
The OC also said one lane near the Ashari Char Bridge was closed on Friday for repair work but was reopened on Saturday morning after the work was completed.

item.title: Home minister announces Tk2 L reward for information on looted, illegal arms
item.description:
Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed has announced a cash reward of up to Tk200,000 for information leading to the recovery of looted and illegal weapons.
He also warned that police officers who fail to make progress within set deadlines in controlling terrorism, extortion and drugs will face strict legal and administrative action.
The minister made the remarks while briefing journalists on Saturday following a “Quarterly Crime Review Meeting” at the Rajarbagh Police Auditorium.
Salahuddin said police would undertake targeted efforts to recover looted and illegal weapons, with a special police unit being formed for the purpose.
To encourage people to assist in recovering the weapons, the government has announced rewards of up to Tk200,000, he said.
At the meeting, police members raised various issues concerning law and order, including the need for increased technological support in their work.
The home minister said the government was working on these matters and issued necessary directives to maintain the law-and-order situation.
Responding to journalists’ questions after the meeting, he said police had been instructed that the law-and-order situation would gradually improve further.

item.title: Justice Habibul Gani to take oath as Appellate Division judge Sunday
item.description:
Newly appointed Appellate Division judge Justice Md Habibul Gani will take oath at 9:30am on Sunday, with Chief Justice Zubayer Rahman Chowdhury scheduled to administer the oath.
The Supreme Court’s Public Relations Officer Md Shafiqul Islam said this in a notice issued on Saturday.
President appointed Justice Md Habibul Gani, a judge of the High Court Division, to the Appellate Division on Thursday. A gazette notification was subsequently issued on his appointment.
Justice Habibul Gani has served in the High Court Division since 2011. His orders and judgments in several important cases have included a case concerning the Dhaka University Central Students’ Union (Ducsu) election.
With his appointment, the Appellate Division now has five judges, including the chief justice.
